brief:
Joel's published two paragraphs, which the detector flagged:
«Look at Google Trends for “ecovillage” and “intentional community.” Interest had been drifting downward for years, then bent upward sharply in the mid-2020s.»

«I can’t prove AI caused that turn. The timing is still hard to ignore. Around the same period, AI stopped being a tech-news curiosity and began reorganizing people’s jobs, feeds, relationships, and expectations of the future. Suddenly “maybe we should form a village” sounded less like a 1972 leftover and more like a backup plan.»

Carry everything in it: every claim at the same strength, every condition and hedge, the same people doing the same things, and nothing new about Joel's life or anyone else's. Write it in your own sentences, not his, except the words marked to keep. Don't add examples, reasons or feelings that aren't in his paragraph.

Keep word for word:
- “ecovillage” and “intentional community”, each in quotation marks (each carries a link)
- the second paragraph’s last sentence, word for word: Suddenly “maybe we should form a village” sounded less like a 1972 leftover and more like a backup plan.

Also: All four of what AI began reorganizing stay: jobs, feeds, relationships, and expectations of the future.
before: Whether you want to call that loneliness an official “epidemic” or not, it’s obvious that a lot of people can’t tolerate modern life in isolation anymore. They may disagree about politics, food, God, sex, or whether shoes are oppressive, but they agree that something about the current arrangement is starvin’ them.
after: It’s poppin’ on Instagram too! 🔥 Chantress Seba—my favorite light-language love influencer—posted an application for people interested in starting a commune. I applied, although I don’t think she’s coming to Africa. When I saw the post, many thousands of people appeared to be interested. Imagine opening your inbox after casually inviting a million followers to co-found a village.
length: the first paragraph one or two sentences, 20 to 40 words; the second three or four sentences, 45 to 75 words
voice: in Joel's voice, like the paragraphs around it (first person where he speaks for himself)
